lead.headline: The Sensex jumps 2.7% to a three-month high as oil crashes 9% after the Democrats' sweep
lead.short: The Sensex was up 2.7% at 79,372 at 2pm on Thursday, its highest in three months, after Brent crude fell about 9% on Wednesday to around $94 a barrel. Traders are betting that a Democratic Congress will push Donald Trump to wind down the Iran war. The rally added nearly ₹8 lakh crore to the value of BSE companies.

why.text: India imports most of its oil, so a $10 fall in crude eases the rupee, inflation and company costs at once.

more: The Nifty 50 crossed 24,000 for the first time since 4 September and was up 2.5% at 24,554 at 2pm, with bank shares up 3.3%; it is the market's sixth straight rising session. Foreign investors bought ₹7,284 crore of Indian shares on Wednesday, their biggest single day since October 2025 and their fourth day of buying in a row. The S&P 500 hit a three-month high overnight.

US energy shares fell nearly 5% as Democrats who won in Texas and Georgia had campaigned against new data centres, a big source of expected gas demand. Some analysts warn the defeat could push Trump towards escalation instead. "If Tehran recognises that Trump needs a deal, but not just any deal, a genuine opportunity could emerge to end the war," said Ebtesam al-Ketbi of the Emirates Policy Center.

update.new: A 2.7% surge as oil crashes after the midterms.
update.front: The midterm result has done more for Indian markets in a day than weeks of Iran talks.

seconds.headline: JD Vance says the Iran war is 'the reason we lost', in a rare public break with Trump, who says he would do it again
seconds.short: Vice-President JD Vance blamed the Republicans' midterm defeat on the Iran war in a 600-word statement on X on Wednesday, widely read as distancing himself from Donald Trump before a possible 2028 run. "The reason we lost is the war," he wrote. Trump agreed the war had "largely" decided the vote, but said he would "do it again".

why.text: A split at the top over the war makes a US exit from it, and lower oil prices, more likely.

more: "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest," Vance wrote. He has publicly backed the war since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February, but has reportedly opposed it in private meetings.

It is hard to recall a sitting vice-president breaking so sharply with a president on a signature foreign policy, the BBC says. Trump, who prizes loyalty, was mild: "I know how he feels about it. I think it was fine." Angry Republicans are blaming Trump for what one called "a disaster", and Senator Ted Cruz has also signalled a fight inside the party.

facts.Vance: "The reason we lost is the war"

update.new: Vance blames the war for the defeat.
update.front: The vice-president has turned on the war in public, the first crack at the top of the administration.

seconds.headline: Joshua Wong, the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, is jailed for another 10 years for colluding with foreign forces
seconds.short: Joshua Wong was sentenced on Thursday to 10 years in prison for colluding with foreign forces under Hong Kong's national security law. Wong, 30, has already spent six years in jail and was due to be freed in January. He pleaded guilty in September to conspiring with the exiled activist Nathan Law to lobby for foreign sanctions on Beijing.

why.text: It shows how completely Beijing has closed down dissent in Hong Kong, a city with a large Indian business community.

more: Prosecutors said the lobbying took place between July and late November 2020. Wong and Law co-founded Demosisto, a now-defunct pro-democracy party. Two months and two days of the new term will run alongside his current sentence for subversion. Dozens of Hongkongers queued for hours outside the court for a seat in the public gallery, under a heavy police presence.

Chief executive John Lee called Wong and Law "among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong's prosperity and stability". Hundreds of campaigners and ordinary residents have been arrested under the law imposed in 2020 after mass protests. Critics say it has silenced dissent; the authorities say it is needed for stability.

seconds.headline: Burglars steal former India hockey captain MM Somaya's 1980 Olympic gold medal from his Bengaluru home
seconds.short: Two burglars broke into the New Thippasandra home of former India hockey captain M.M. Somaya at about 2.34am on 28 October and took his 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal, other international medals, jewellery and cash, police say. The family was away in Kodagu. Indiranagar police have formed two special teams to find the thieves.

why.text: It is the medal from India's last Olympic gold in men's hockey, and it was taken from a house in the city.

more: "One of the medals stolen is India's last Olympic Gold Medal in men's hockey," Somaya said, calling it "an irreplaceable symbol of years of dedication, sacrifice and service to the country". Neighbours noticed the open door at about 7.15am, and CCTV from a nearby house shows two men breaking in.

The thieves also took his silver from the 1982 Asian Games in Delhi, two bronze medals and silver cups, gold bangles and coins, and ₹30,000 in cash, worth an estimated ₹3.53 lakh in all. Somaya played at three Olympics, captained India at Seoul in 1988 and received the Arjuna Award in 1985.

facts.stolen: 1980 Moscow Olympics gold and other medals

seconds.headline: The US sanctions an Indian couple, two other Indians and nine firms for helping ships carry Iranian oil
seconds.short: The US Treasury on Wednesday sanctioned what it called "the vast criminal network" of India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, two other Indian citizens who run their businesses, and nine connected entities, along with firms in Türkiye. Treasury says they gave false flags and certificates to sanctioned ships carrying Iranian petroleum.

why.text: It puts Indian shipping firms in the line of fire just as Washington hints at easing tariffs on India.

more: The sanctions are part of what the administration calls "Operation Economic Outcast", aimed at cutting off Iran's oil sales. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the Treasury said.

False flags and fake maritime certificates let ships dodge safety and environmental rules and sail without insurance. The move came a day after Democrats won Congress. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has hinted that the 25% tariff on India over Russian oil could come off as Indian refiners buy less of it: "I would imagine there is a path to take them off."

stories.headline: Kerala-born Nithya Raman defeats Karen Bass to become mayor of Los Angeles
stories.short: Nithya Raman, an Indian-origin city councillor first elected in 2020, has defeated the incumbent Karen Bass to win the mayoralty of Los Angeles, the second-biggest city in the United States. She challenged Bass in February, weeks after endorsing her, and campaigned on homelessness, housing and public safety with the backing of the Democratic Socialists of America.

why.text: An Indian-origin mayor now runs America's second-biggest city.

more: Raman has pledged to halve street homelessness by the summer of 2028 and end it by the close of her first four-year term, calling Bass's approach costly and ineffective. Bass, a former member of Congress, had the backing of most of the city's establishment, including the county Federation of Labor and the county Democratic Party.

Bass won only 34% in the June primary, a weak showing for an incumbent, and her ratings stayed low after the 2025 Palisades fire broke out while she was abroad. In the final days Raman campaigned at bars, nightclubs and colleges, while Bass toured senior centres. Pia Dandiya also won a House seat in Florida.

stories.headline: Valverde scores in stoppage time as Real Madrid come from behind twice to win 3-2 at AEK Athens
stories.short: Real Madrid won 3-2 at AEK Athens on Wednesday to keep their perfect Champions League record, with captain Federico Valverde scoring the winner deep into stoppage time. Jude Bellingham equalised with a backheel in the 32nd minute and Kylian Mbappé made it 2-2 before Valverde, on as a substitute, settled it. It was Madrid's seventh straight win.

why.text: Madrid stay perfect in Europe and on a long winning run before Saturday's trip to Valencia.

more: Valverde made the most of his 28 minutes, creating three chances and making nine progressive passes, Managing Madrid's data shows. Bernardo Silva and Bellingham each made 17 progressive passes and seven carries, and Mbappé generated the most threat from open-play passes and took shots worth 1.38 expected goals.

Eduardo Camavinga made a match-high 18 defensive actions in 94 minutes. Madrid had nine of the top 10 players for expected threat from open play, while AEK had six of the top 10 for defensive actions. The club have also named Rafael Nadal to their board of directors. Madrid visit Valencia on Saturday night.

stories.headline: Djokovic loses to qualifier Rinky Hijikata in Paris and misses the ATP Finals, while Alcaraz reaches the third round
stories.short: Novak Djokovic lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata, ranked 83rd, in the Paris Masters second round on Wednesday, ending his hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin. Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex Michelsen 7-6, 6-3 and plays Matteo Berrettini on Court Central at 23:30 IST tonight.

why.text: Djokovic's season is over, and Alcaraz is the big name left in Paris.

more: Djokovic, 39, has missed the Finals only twice in 20 seasons when fit. He looked laboured as Hijikata raised his level, and said his plan for the next few weeks is "just rest". "He was switched on, I wasn't serving as well and he was just playing out of his mind, honestly," Djokovic said. He has not reached a Masters quarter-final this year.

It was a day of upsets: world No. 1 Alexander Zverev lost to Lorenzo Musetti and Daniil Medvedev to Ignacio Buse, though both have already qualified for Turin. Alex de Minaur lost to Tomás Martín Etcheverry, and Frances Tiafoe to Quentin Halys, leaving Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul chasing the last two places.

update.new: Djokovic is out and misses Turin; Alcaraz is through.
